acceptanceCriteria: A worker whose only non-ignored children are sleeping with no CPU-time advance since the previous tick is stopped with reason IDLE after idleSeconds; a child that is runnable or whose CPU time advanced still marks the worker busy; each with a focused regression test (run with -race).
The owning spec carries numbered requirements for the busy-child rule, marked proposed pending owner acceptance.
body:
Source: GitHub beamfall/corvint#793. Refs #793.

Observed: `corvint-tasks dispatch` never stops a worker for `idleSeconds` when the agent host keeps long-lived helper processes (agent server child, MCP servers) in the worker's process tree. `busyChild` treats any non-leader member whose `comm` is not in `idleIgnore` as busy regardless of activity, so `LastActive` is refreshed every tick and the IDLE branch is unreachable. 0 IDLE kills over ~670 kills with idleSeconds 900; a hung worker (log silent 25+ min, all members sleeping <0.5% CPU) ran to wallSeconds.

Expected: a worker whose log, activity paths and child processes show no progress for `idleSeconds` is stopped with reason IDLE. A child counts as busy only when it is runnable or its CPU time advanced since the last tick, not merely because it exists.

Workaround: list helper command names in `idleIgnore`.

Tests named in the PR: CAL-V0-218 dispatch idle busy-child tests. Doc gates, repin check, independent review and dogfood bind/check/seal reported PASS in the PR. make gate NOT_RUN (owner scoped-work preference); native claim unavailable (COVERAGE_UNKNOWN/RESOURCE_COLLISION). title: dispatch idleSeconds never fires when workers keep long-lived helper processes (GH #793)
